text:
maya: Quick RFC follow-up — cohorting vs per-tenant queues for the continuous batching scheduler. Wanted to capture tradeoffs we didn't finish yesterday.
raj: TL;DR: per-tenant queues = stronger isolation, but big perf hit for small tenants. Cohorts (size buckets) = better utilization, weaker isolation.
liam: Agree. Main question: where do we draw the line for latency critical tenants?
sophia: We also need to factor KV-cache affinity. If we split too much, cache locality goes away and cold kv loads kill 99.9 latency.
ana: +1 on cache affinity. Also: admission credits + headroom token model might help keep small-tenants fast without max-per-tenant queues.
maya: Idea: hybrid topology — use per-tenant micro-lanes for SLA-tiered tenants, and cohorted lanes for everything else. Admission policy decides routing.
raj: That's basically what I sketched in the whiteboard. Implementation concern: mixing topologies complicates the admission surface and metrics.
liam: Implementation sketch: each request gets (tenant_id, sla_tag, seq_len_hint). Router consults: if sla_tag == "p99-critical" -> micro-lane else -> cohort based on seq_len_hint.
sophia: For cohorts we should bucket by seq_len percentiles + payload size. Avoid creating too many buckets. 3-5 cohorts seems enough.
ana: Also track KV cache hit ratio per cohort. If a cohort's cache-hit drops below threshold, we either merge it back or warm caches differently.
maya: Preemption question: Should micro-lanes be preemptible by global emergency lanes? e.g., when capacity constrained, evict cohort work first or micro-lane first?
raj: For fairness, prefer preempt cohort work before micro-lane for SLA tenants. But we need graceful fallback — fallback to a smaller model or higher-latency variant.
liam: Fallbacks need route-level config. Example: "if latency > X and capacity < Y -> route to compact-quantized model". We should codify that in rollout config.
sophia: Observability hooks: per-lane p50/p95/p99, kv-cache-hit, batch-size distribution, latency-by-seq. Without these, debugging will be painful.
ana: Telemetry note: we'll need tenant-tagged histograms and cohort-tagged metrics. Also correlate with 'model-variant' to reason about fallbacks.
maya: Another tradeoff: batching window size. Cohorts can tolerate larger windows (higher throughput) but micro-lanes must keep windows tiny. So we'd need separate windowing parameters per lane.
raj: That implies the runtime needs multi-window scheduler — not just one global coalescer. Is that a big refactor?
liam: Moderate. We already have hooks for variable windowing in coalesce operator. Need clearer operator boundary + per-lane configs.
sophia: Side effect: more knobs = complexity for users. Provide sane defaults and an "auto" mode that tunes windows based on observed latency curves.
maya: Action item: Sophia, can you draft observability matrix? Raj/ Liam, draft a runtime surface for hybrid-lanes (API + config). Ana, draft admission policy pseudocode.
ana: Will do. Quick pseudocode snippet now:
```
if tenant.sla == CRITICAL:
  lane = micro_lane(tenant)
else:
  lane = cohort_bucket(seq_len_estimate, size_estimate)
admit = check_admission(lane, credits, headroom)
```
raj: Also test edge case: a single tenant with bursty traffic crossing cohorts — ensure we don't oscillate their routing and thrash caches.
liam: Add hysteresis to cohort promotions/demotions. e.g., require sustained pattern for 30s before moving tenant.
maya: Sounds good. Last thought: we should simulate with our trace-replay tool before any rollout. Use 10x load and faulty-kv scenarios.
sophia: I can extend the trace harness to tag tenants and emulate KV cold starts.
ana: I'll prototype admission-credit model with a simple token-bucket + headroom multiplier and share numbers.
maya: Cool — let's reconvene in two days with PRs/notes. @deploy-bot can you schedule a 30m deep-dive on calendar? :calendar: 
deploy-bot: Meeting created: "Hybrid lanes deep-dive — continuous batching" on Thu 11:00 (invites: maya, raj, liam, sophia, ana).
maya: Thanks. Also please add the whiteboard screenshot to the thread (uploaded). :eyes:
raj: Uploaded a short spike script too under /infra/batching/spikes for anyone who wants to run local sims.
liam: I'll run the sim and post results here once done.
sophia: Filing follow-up RFC doc with decisions + open items. Will ping when ready. :memo:
